coaching.headline: Objective control decided this: Aurora took the last Fangtooth, both Primal Fangtooths, the Shaper and Orb Prime; every won fight became a prize.

flags.text: Greystone was a hell of an anchor: game-high 87664 mitigated, four kills on Zarus, and destroyed the Core.
The enemy won four fights but converted only one, and no allied inhibitor fell all game.
Aurora and Riktor as tanks against zero enemy tanks: the sounder shape, 52.8% against 48.1% in ranked.
Riktor's deaths were the ugly part: eight, split three to Mourn, three to Sparrow, two to Countess.

focus.title: Keep converting, stop the duo bleed
focus.action: Keep turning every won fight into the nearest structure or major. Before minute ten, Murdock and Riktor trade into Sparrow and Mourn only with Aurora on the duo side.

23.call: Picks across mid, offlane, duo and the allied jungle went 4-0 as Greystone razed the enemy offlane outer, then Aurora took Fangtooth. Repeat that order: picks, nearest tower, pit.

10.5.call: Two separate plays: Zarus killed Greystone on the offlane, Mourn and Sparrow killed Riktor and Iggy & Scorch on the duo side, then the enemy took Fangtooth. Avoid trades on both sides while Fangtooth stands.

26.5.call: With Aurora dead to Serath, Greystone killed Zarus on the offlane while Sparrow killed Riktor and Murdock on the duo side. With the jungler down, the duo backs off Sparrow.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Game-high 33932 healing and 12.2 CS a minute against an own average of 8.9. Whenever Zarus is dead, push the offlane wave into the next tower.
Hero damage 1014 a minute against an own average of 578, with two deaths all game. In late fights, keep starting on the closest diver: Countess, Zarus or Serath.
14a156f5-ee4c-412f-898b-bd164cc33f6f: Sixteen kills and 35479 objective damage, both the game's most, with five kills on Mourn. After each pick on the duo side, hit the nearest tower before resetting.
Six of seven deaths went to Sparrow, three outside any detected fight, a shit pattern. Until Sparrow shows elsewhere, farm the duo side with the support near.
Heightened Senses is Sparrow's only escape, a brief stealth with no dash: save Static Trap for after that stealth, and never hide behind walls from Piercing Shot.
79964e3a-0d53-4617-ab3a-427130f2bd7c: Secured the first Fangtooth; duo-lane rotation kills on Sparrow and Countess answered two allied deaths. Before the mid outer falls, rotate only when the duo is already fighting.
Razed the enemy mid outer, mid inner and a duo inhibitor. Whenever a won fight exposes the next mid structure, keep taking that siege first.
Deaths ran 44% over an own average, three to Sparrow. In fights, cast Inferno only after Riktor's Skewer lands, with Riktor and Aurora between Sparrow and the backline.
55bc9d9e-e2c0-4963-9088-4120d1bb6dd9: Took 130 enemy-jungle minions and placed 9 wards against an own average of 6.2, with 13 assists. When Serath shows on another lane, keep taking the enemy camps.
Both deaths came outside any detected fight, to Zarus early and to Serath later. Before invading, ward the entrance and confirm where Serath is.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Ran the vision: 17 wards against an own average of 6, tied with Mourn for the game's most, and 45% kill participation. Hold that ward rate before every Fangtooth.
Deaths ran 66% over an own average; the duo lost six deaths to one before minute ten. When Mourn channels Beguile, step out of the light first.

matchup: Countess was the lane opponent, a 51.7% matchup over 270 games, and died a game-high nine times.
Countess's Feast suppresses; Sparrow, the game's top hero damage dealer, scored three of the five deaths.
build: Tainted Bastion and Tainted Guard cut the attacker's healing when hit by magic damage and by basic attacks, respectively.
Spellbreaker blocks the next ability with a spell shield.
Wraith Leggings, finished last, was absent from the earlier fights.
eternal: Vesh turns a share of ability damage on heroes into damage over time; Mind Rot adds current-health damage.
Aion and Lotus lead a toss-up in this mid field; Vesh, the most played, ranks well behind.
The Tenth Seal with Mind Rot trails Lich with Mind Rot, the best Vesh pair.
augment: Hold This! makes the Molotov explosion permanently stronger against heroes each time the explosion hits one.
Turret Maniac and Badlands Belch lead a toss-up in this mid field; Hold This! ranks third.
crest: Nyr Warboots adds health and both armors; the active grants decaying speed and brief max-health regeneration.
Soulbearer is clearly best in this mid field; Nyr Warboots has too few games to lead.
improvement: Into Countess the field buys Tainted Scepter more than usual, a 51.9% item over 4030 games.
Orb Of Growth, Megacosm and Dreambinder, a 65.2% core over 138 games, appear nowhere in this build.
Turret Maniac over Hold This! is the field-backed augment swap: a fourth turret at lower turret health.

matchup: Zarus was the lane opponent, a 53.6% matchup over 550 games; four of seven Zarus deaths came from this offlane.
Zarus razed the allied offlane outer, the first structure the team lost.
build: Overlord, Augmentation and Mutilator all stacked on basic attacks, and 45 ability haste brought Stone Forged Soul back 31% sooner.
Tainted Blade cuts healing on physical damage, answering Countess, Zarus and Mourn, the three self-healing enemy kits.
Rebirth, finished after the second death, never had a death to answer.
eternal: Krix adds max health and size by level; Cannibalism adds permanent max health per takedown.
Nihil and Weald lead a toss-up in this offlane field; Krix, the most played, ranks third.
Voracity with Cannibalism is the best Krix pair; Regenerative Tissue with Cannibalism is the most played.
augment: Tainted Oath makes Sacred Oath apply Blight to enemies.
Tainted Oath leads a toss-up with Imperial Soul in this offlane field. Sound keep.
crest: Saphir's Mantle's active grows size and max health briefly, damages nearby heroes, then adds permanent max health.
Pacifier and Eviscerator lead a toss-up in this offlane field; Saphir's Mantle ranks behind both.
improvement: Rapture completes the strongest listed core, 65.8% over 158 games, alongside the owned Overlord and Forticus.
Anti-heal was already covered by Tainted Blade; no other change is proven by this match.

matchup: Duo faced Sparrow and Mourn; the carry matchup into Sparrow is 46.2% over 1712 games, and Sparrow drew first blood.
Sparrow dealt a game-high 76397 hero damage and built Vanquisher and Demolisher for armor penetration.
Five kills on Mourn and four on Sparrow, spread across both jungles, the duo lane and the enemy base.
build: Lightning Hawk, Tainted Rounds and Imperator match the strongest listed core, 60.4% over 712 games.
Vanquisher executes heroes taken below a small health threshold; Terminus turns lifesteal overhealing into a shield.
Lightning Hawk was finished last, so earlier fights ran without Lightning Hawk.
eternal: Weald fires true-damage missiles on damaging a hero below a health threshold; Dryad's Boon shortens basic ability cooldowns on hit.
Xyris, Demiurge and Thraex lead a toss-up in this carry field; Weald ranks fifth.
Forage with Taproot is the best Weald pair; Dryad's Boon with Taproot trails.
augment: Justice's Reach makes Shots Fired pierce units and adds range.
Justice's Reach is clearly best in this carry field. Sound keep.
crest: Pacifier's active is a short dash plus an empowered physical hit that grows on low-health targets and can recast after hero kills.
Pacifier leads a toss-up with Exodus in this carry field; Pacifier carries no armor.
improvement: Physical armor was the unmet need: Sparrow scored six of seven deaths, and no item or crest here carries any.
When Sparrow leads the enemy damage, trade one late damage slot for physical armor; the cost is kill pressure.

matchup: Serath was the jungle opponent, a 53.2% matchup over 438 games; Serath took all three Seedlings and the enemy Fangtooth.
Kills landed on Countess twice and on Zarus and Serath once each.
build: Magnify matches the strongest listed core; Prophecy and Orion, the other two pieces, were not built.
Elafrost empowers the next basic attack after a cast with area damage and a slow.
Crystalline Cuirass, finished last, missed the earlier fights.
eternal: Krix adds max health and size by level; Predator grants bonus damage and speed after camp leader kills, longer on epic monsters.
Nihil is clearly best in this jungle field; Krix ranks last among the ranked Eternals.
Regenerative Tissue with Predator, as run, is the best Krix pair.
augment: Hypothermia makes Boreal Sweep shred both armors and slow attack speed on enemy heroes.
Hypothermia leads a toss-up with Glacial Thorns in this jungle field. Sound keep.
crest: Tempest's active damages nearby heroes each second and heals for a share of the damage.
Epoch leans first in this jungle field, Saphir's Mantle second; Tempest, the most played, ranks behind both.
improvement: Anti-heal was the unmet need against Countess, Zarus and Mourn; Tainted Guard or Tainted Bastion would answer.
Nihil for Krix is the field's clear lean: power and armor that build during hero fights, over flat max health.

matchup: Duo faced Mourn and Sparrow; Mourn wins this lane 52.2% of the time.
Mourn's Abduct pulls; Countess's Feast suppresses, and Countess scored two early kills on this support.
build: Forticus, Tainted Guard and Transference, a 58% core over 138 games, appear nowhere in this build.
Dynamo makes an immobilized enemy take more damage briefly; Xenia shields allies standing close.
Cursed Scroll, finished last, missed the earlier fights.
eternal: Krix adds max health and size by level; Regenerative Tissue restores max health after a stretch without hero damage.
Knell, Lotus and Idrisil lead a toss-up in this support field; Krix, the most played, ranks lower.
Regenerative Tissue with Cannibalism is the best Krix pair, as run.
augment: Wanton Warden regenerates health equal to a share of damage taken, rising with level.
Zap O' 9-Chains leans ahead of Wanton Warden in this support field.
crest: Sanctification's active shields self and nearby heroes, adding tenacity while the shield holds; Visionary raises the ward cap.
Reclamation leans first in this support field; Rift Walkers also ranks above Sanctification.
improvement: Anti-heal was the unmet need against Countess, Zarus and Mourn; Tainted Guard, part of the listed core, answers.
Zap O' 9-Chains over Wanton Warden is the field lean: an area zap after casts, giving up regeneration from damage taken.

threats: Chain-CC risk (2 hard-CC abilities, ~1.3s of lockdown): Countess Feast (suppress 0.75s), Mourn Abduct (pull). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Mourn. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought 3 items of it.
Dive threat on our backline: Serath, Countess. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Iggy & Scorch Inferno (knockback), Riktor Riplash (pull), Riktor Shock Therapy (silence 0.8s), Riktor Skewer (suppress 1.25s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Riktor) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Oil Spill to slow, Molotov to ignite the oil, Flame Turrets to keep shooting, then Inferno and its knockback belch.
ourKits.winCondition: Layer oil, fire and turrets on a choke or objective and burn the team that has to stand in it.
ourKits.passive: Badlands Critter basics stack Slick, a slow that lets his fire ignite the target.
ourKits.playWith: CC that holds enemies in his fire and oil.
ourKits.playAgainst: Do not fight in his oil and fire; flank around it. Melee basics break Flame Turrets quickly, and turrets go inactive when he moves away from them, so drag the fight off them; magical armor helps.

ourKits.combo: Assault The Gates leap in, Make Way to shred armor, Sacred Oath empowered cleave to slow, then Stone Forged Soul to heal in Stasis and crash down.
ourKits.winCondition: Stay in the middle of fights and use Stone Forged Soul's missing-health heal to reset, while Make Way shreds armor for the team.
ourKits.passive: Stoicism deflects the next basic attack on a cooldown and grants health regen and armor that grow as he loses health.
ourKits.playWith: Damage dealers who can follow his leap and benefit from Make Way's armor shred.
ourKits.playAgainst: Do not burst into Stone Forged Soul's Stasis; step away from the slow and the crash, then re-engage. Open with an ability since Stoicism deflects a basic, and buy anti-heal to cut the ult heal.

ourKits.combo: Root a target with Static Trap, shred armor with Buckshot, stack attack speed with Hot Pursuit and finish with the long-range Charged shot or Long Arm of the Law.
ourKits.winCondition: Control space with traps and out-range enemies with Charged basic attacks, then snipe low targets anywhere with Long Arm of the Law.
ourKits.passive: Shots Fired: after 5 landed basic attacks his next one gains extra range and bonus damage.
ourKits.playWith: A frontline or peeling support, since his only escape tools are Buckshot's push back and Hot Pursuit's speed.
ourKits.playAgainst: Avoid fighting over Static Traps and engage after Buckshot is used, since it is his push-back peel. Stay out of the ult line at low health; armor does not help against Long Arm of the Law.

ourKits.combo: Glacial Charge dashes in, Boreal Sweep slows, Hoarfrost roots enemies that touch the ring, then Cryoseism slows and stuns a target before it explodes
ourKits.winCondition: chain slow, root and stun to lock fights down while her Frost Storm grinds max-health damage
ourKits.passive: jumping mid-air leaps her and leaves a Replica that draws tower aggro; hitting a Hero or Monster 4 times summons a Frost Storm
ourKits.playWith: burst damage that turns her long CC chain into kills
ourKits.playAgainst: do not walk into the Hoarfrost ring while it persists; Cryoseism slows before it stuns, so cleanse or tenacity help, and spread so the explosion does not chain; she is weak once Glacial Charge is down

ourKits.combo: Riplash to pull a hero in, Shock Therapy to break their shield and silence, Electrocute aura for damage and a shield, then Skewer to suppress everyone in front of him.
ourKits.winCondition: Land Riplash and chain silence and suppress so the target cannot fight back while their cooldowns stay frozen.
ourKits.passive: Suspended Sentence: while his abilities immobilize or silence a hero, their cooldowns stop ticking.
ourKits.playWith: Burst that deletes his pulled or suppressed target.
ourKits.playAgainst: Stay behind minions or spaced so Riplash cannot reach you, and fight while it is on cooldown. Tenacity shortens the chain, which also shortens the cooldown freeze.

enemyKits.combo: Piercing Shot poke → Heightened Senses for attack speed → Hail of Arrows slow → Inner Fire barrage
enemyKits.winCondition: stack Relentless with basics and abilities to add max-health damage and melt the frontline in long fights
enemyKits.passive: Relentless stacks on hit and makes her basics deal bonus max-health damage
enemyKits.playWith: peel and a frontline, since her only escape is a short stealth
enemyKits.playAgainst: Heightened Senses is her only escape, a brief stealth with speed and no dash, so hard-engage her after it is used; Piercing Shot passes through terrain, so do not hide behind walls at low health

enemyKits.combo: Ascend to dive onto the backline, Chastise to slow and reset her basic attack, Heaven's Fury to go untargetable and strike, then Heresy for speed, attack speed and true-damage burns.
enemyKits.winCondition: Dive the backline, get the first takedown and chain free Heresy activations from Fallen Grace.
enemyKits.passive: Fallen Grace: hero takedowns drop a visage that, when touched, activates Heresy for free and cuts her basic ability cooldowns.
enemyKits.playWith: A frontline that creates her dive angle and CC that holds targets for her.
enemyKits.playAgainst: Do not waste CC or burst during Heaven's Fury, since she is invulnerable then; hit her as she lands from Ascend. Deny the first kill so she cannot pick up the visage.

enemyKits.combo: Shadow Slip dashes in, Eventide and Blade Siphon hit to apply Haemorrhage, then Feast suppresses the Haemorrhaged target for bonus damage and full healing, with Shadow Slip recast to swap back out
enemyKits.winCondition: Feast a Haemorrhaged squishy for bonus damage, heal it back, and escape through the Shadow swap
enemyKits.passive: hitting a hero with two abilities within a short window applies Haemorrhage, a max-health true-damage bleed
enemyKits.playWith: a team to clean up after her pick
enemyKits.playAgainst: Feast is her engage, so peel or punish after it is spent; note where her Shadow was left, since she can swap back to it; magic armor and anti-heal blunt her Blade Siphon and Feast healing

enemyKits.combo: Evade in → Barricade to block then swing for a stun → Spear of Nyr (bonus damage on low targets) → Coliseum leap to finish
enemyKits.winCondition: leap onto a target with Coliseum for doubled Gladiator power and secure kills to stack permanent power
enemyKits.passive: Gladiator stacks grant physical power and heal him as they fall off after combat
enemyKits.playWith: a team that follows his Coliseum leap onto the target
enemyKits.playAgainst: Barricade only blocks from the front, so hit him from the side or behind and dodge its swing stun; disengage during Coliseum's doubled-power window, and buy armor and anti-heal

enemyKits.combo: Abduct to pull a target in, Beguile to Mesmerize the group, Contagion to heal allies and shred enemy armor, and Eclipse to blind the enemy team's vision and spread Contagion map-wide.
enemyKits.winCondition: Pull a target into his team with Abduct, lock the fight with Beguile and keep allies healthy with Contagion.
enemyKits.passive: Extract: his next basic attack cleaves for bonus damage and restores health.
enemyKits.playWith: Burst damage that punishes his pulled or Mesmerized target and benefits from the armor shred.
enemyKits.playAgainst: Abduct and Beguile are both visible channels that slow Mourn, so sidestep the vines and walk out of the growing Beguile radius before it erupts. Anti-heal blunts Contagion and Extract.

lines: Lead story: Damage well above normal. 1,910 hero damage a minute, more than 98% of Sparrow carry players this patch (43% of the team's). The damage came from Lightning Hawk, Sky Splitter, Tainted Rounds.
Sparrow dealt 76,397 hero damage, 43% of their team's, with +280 physical power from items.

Penetration: Vanquisher 12, Demolisher ignores 25%; against Murdock (level 17 estimated: about 110 physical armor, 70 after penetration) and Riktor (level 17 estimated: about 302 physical armor, 215 after penetration) that is about 23% and 28% more damage (estimate: percent penetration taken before flat).
Lightning Hawk (item): While moving or landing Basic Attacks: Generate stacks of Momentum. At 100 stacks empower your next Basic Attack On-Hit. Deal 40 (+20%) Damage. Slows by 20% for 0.75s.
Sky Splitter (item): On Successful Basic Attacks: Deal 5% of Target's Current Health as Damage On-Hit. Reduced to 3.5% for Ranged Heroes. Minimum of 12 Damage.
Tainted Rounds (item): On Successful Basic Attacks: Reduce the Target's Healing by 45% for 3s. Deal (+10%) (+20%) Damage On-Hit. Increases by up to 100% as the Target's Health decreases.

Sustain: 22% lifesteal; Terminus: On Overhealing from Lifesteal: Convert excess Healing into a Shield. Max Shield size: (+100%). The Shield slowly decays 15s after leaving combat.; 1,037 healing recorded.

Lesson: Sparrow's penetration cut through: Murdock took about 23% more physical damage than their armor alone allows (estimate: at level 17 (estimated) their armor was about 110, about 70 after 12 flat + 25% penetration).
Stack (Every basic attack set off): 4 effects on one trigger: Lightning Hawk, Sky Splitter, Demolisher, Tainted Rounds.
Stack (Healing off the damage): 2 effects on one trigger: Sky Splitter, Terminus.
Stack (Kept alive in fights): 2 effects on one trigger: Demolisher, Terminus. Together they made staying in a long fight cheaper: more armor, shields or healing the longer it went.
Countered? 2 of the 3 players Sparrow killed built physical armor (Iggy & Scorch, Riktor). Anti-heal on Iggy & Scorch, Greystone, Murdock. We killed Sparrow 6 times.
Copy it? Too few Sparrow carry games with this Eternal or core this patch to say whether it wins elsewhere.

lines: Lead story: Healed through fights. 848 healing a minute, more than 98% of Greystone offlane players this patch.
Stone Forged Soul at top rank: 145s base, about 100s by the end (31% shorter) from 45 ability haste: Tainted Blade 10, Augmentation 20, Mutilator 15.
Their build heals off damage: anti-heal (the Tainted items) cuts it.
Greystone dealt 40,561 hero damage, 24% of their team's, with +195 physical power from items.
Overlord (item): On Successful Basic Attack: Deal (+1%) Damage. Deal (+30%) (+2.5%) Damage around the Target. Damage decreases from 100% to 50% based on distance.
Tainted Blade (item): On dealing Physical Damage: Reduce the Target's Healing by 45% for 3s.
Tainted Blade (item): On dealing Ability Damage to a Blighted Target: Cause them to take 5% more damage for 3s.
Augmentation (item): On Ability Cast: Empower your next Basic Attack within 4s. Deal (+90% Base Physical Power) Damage On-Hit.
Forticus (item): Upon taking Hero damage: Gain a (+8%) Shield for 3.5s.
Forticus (item): Upon damaging or being damaged by Heroes: For the next 3s, gain Stats each second: (+0.6% Base Health) additional Max Health, +4 Movement Speed and +0.5% Size.
Mutilator (item): On Successsful Basic Attacks: Deal 1% of their Max Health as Damage.
Sustain: 12% omnivamp; Forticus: Upon taking Hero damage: Gain a (+8%) Shield for 3.5s.; Forticus: Shield Activations: Hero Combat Time:; 33,932 healing recorded.
Toughness: +1350 health, +55 physical armor, +25% tenacity; took 78,429 damage, mitigated 87,664, died 2 times.
Stack (Every basic attack set off): 3 effects on one trigger: Overlord, Augmentation, Mutilator.

Stack (Every ability hit set off): 2 effects on one trigger: Tainted Blade, Mutilator. Greystone has 4 damaging abilities (Assault The Gates, Make Way, Sacred Oath, Stone Forged Soul hit an area, so one cast sets them off on several heroes), and 45 ability haste brought them back 31% sooner: more casts, more triggers.
Stack (Kept alive in fights): 2 effects on one trigger: Forticus, Mutilator. Together they made staying in a long fight cheaper: more armor, shields or healing the longer it went.
Countered? 1 of the 2 players Greystone killed built physical armor (Zarus). Anti-heal on Sparrow, Zarus. We killed Greystone 2 times.
Copy it? Too few Greystone offlane games with this Eternal or core this patch to say whether it wins elsewhere.

bullets: Heightened Senses' attack speed crammed more basic attacks into 6s, and each landed basic attack added Relentless's max-health bonus and Sky Splitter's 3.5% current-health hit.
Weald fired true-damage missiles after Sparrow damaged a low-health hero, on a per-hero cooldown; Wind-Rider added attack speed leaving Heightened Senses' Stealth; Forage added farm gold and XP.
Tainted Rounds cut the target's healing by 45% for 3s on each landed basic attack, with bonus damage growing as the target's health dropped.
Augmentation empowered the next basic attack within 4s after an ability cast, on a short cooldown; that swing set off Overlord's splash and Mutilator's 1% max-health hit.
Krix's bonus max health and Cannibalism's permanent health per takedown made Stone Forged Soul's max-health heal bigger; Regenerative Tissue restored health after time without taking hero damage.
Forticus shielded Greystone on taking hero damage, on a cooldown, and grew max health, movement speed and size for 3s after trading damage with heroes.
After 5 landed basic attacks, Shots Fired gave the next one 400 more range and bonus damage; Sky Splitter and Tainted Rounds landed on each basic attack.
Weald's minors worked on every basic attack hit: Dryad's Boon trimmed Buckshot, Static Trap and Hot Pursuit cooldowns, and Taproot restored Murdock's health, except when hitting towers.
Weald fired true-damage missiles after Murdock damaged a low-health hero, on a per-hero cooldown, while Tainted Rounds hit harder as the target's health dropped.
